Piaseczno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Piaseczno, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Piaseczno developed through the 19th century; by 1921, 2,256 Jews made up 40% of the town's population, deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in January 1941 and mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery was likely established between 1866 and 1870, replacing burials previously conducted 16km away in Kajetany. During the war, Germans executed about 30 Warsaw Jews here in 1943, followed by Warsaw Uprising insurgents in 1944. In the 1990s, the Foundation of Eternal Remembrance, local authorities, and area schoolchildren cleaned up the undeveloped portion of the site.
